text: Seat-7, Elsa. You've lit your stall and said nothing while the rest of us trade words like copper and lead. What did you see in the dark before the braziers were lit?

Seat-3, Yoda (3), you talked of shadows and shutters but gave no proof. Tell me plain: did you shutter a stall last night? Yes or no. No lantern, no loom—just the braziers' light on the ledger. Who did you vote to banish in the dark?

Seat-7, Elsa (7), you ignored my first question. Now I ask again: What did you see in the dark before the braziers were lit? Silence is copper turned to lead in this bazaar.

Seat-9, Inigo (9), your kettle of words boils but pours nothing. Did you shutter a stall last night? The ledger waits.

Seat-5, Ripley (5), your spice and iron stink of guesswork. Prove your scent or step aside. Who benefits from your accusation?

Speak plain or shut your stall.

Seat-8, Morpheus (8). You measured the bazaar’s fire but left the metal unnamed. Did you shutter a stall last night? Yes or no. The kiln doesn’t care for poetry—it wants the weight of copper, not alloy. Yoda (3), your lantern swings bright but your own knot is loose—you demanded yes or no from every seat and gave none yourself. Did you shutter a stall last night? Yes or no. Ripley (5), your spice and iron stink of guesswork; the bazaar’s scales only weigh what’s placed on them. Name the stall or step aside. Elsa (7), your birds speak in riddles—what did you see in the dark before the braziers were lit? The night watch leaves no room for metaphors. Hermione (2), your warp threads hum steady, but steady looms do not weave when the shuttle is missing. If you are not the Doctor, then what lantern lights your stall? Gandalf (1), an empty ledger is not clean—it’s unread. Did you shutter a stall last night? Yes or no. The bazaar’s ink runs dry when silence is the only currency traded.
